subject: Audit replay & temporary retention: pilot evidence handoff proposal
thread_content:
From: David Ramos <dramos@helixhealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Helix Health Security <security@helixhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary longer audit window for pilot + access model

Hey Markus —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we dig into the pilot scope we hit a blocker on evidence retention: our compliance team requires a 90-day complete audit window for any workflow that touches patient identifiers (even pseudonymized). For the pilot (small user set) we asked if Redwood can temporarily hold a separate, short-term "audit replay" bundle that includes request/response logs plus the KV cache snapshot.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- export a time-bounded audit bundle (90 days) separated from standard retention buckets
- provide read-only access to that bundle via S3 link to our secure bucket or transfer to our KMS escrow for the duration
- provide a short proof-of-fulfillment (signed) when the bundle is handed back or destroyed

I've attached a small sample of the logs we expect (audit-log-sample.csv) and a quick sketch of our suggested workflow.

Appreciate a quick reality check — pilot needs sign-off by end of next week.

—David
Security Operations
Helix Health


-----Original Message-----
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: David Ramos <dramos@helixhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marucs_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary longer audit window for pilot + access model

David —

Thanks for the concrete ask and the sample. Quick summary of constraints from our side:
- Hosted customers use our standard retention tiers (30 / 90 / 365) but for pilot we typically recommend ephemeral escrow with customer-managed S3 + temporary ledger export.
- We can generate an "audit replay" bundle that includes request/response logs, KV snapshot, and a tokenized trace, but there are two operational trade-offs: (1) bucket encryption — if you want the bundle encrypted under your KMS key we need BYOK handoff earlier in the flow; (2) replay fidelity — we can scrub PII but that may make regresses harder to debug.

Questions for the team (cc'd):
- Kimberly: what are the engineering steps to produce a one-off bundle pinned to a date range and push it to an external S3 under customer KMS? Estimated T-shirt: which sprint?
- Marcus: account ops — can we treat this as a temporary exception under the pilot SLA and create a special retention tag so it doesn't get included in normal audit exports?

David, if we can get a small MOU/Docusign that covers the short-term escrow and destruction confirmation, we should be able to do this without product changes (ops + a little infra work). I attached a diff doc with the proposed retention-handling steps.

—Markus
Senior Product Manager, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference


On Wed, Oct 07, 2026 at 13:20, kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, David Ramos <dramos@helixhealth.com>
Cc: marucs_lin@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 13:20:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary longer audit window for pilot + access model

Thanks Markus, David — added a little more detail from an implementation standpoint.

Operational plan (draft):
1) One-off bundle generator: infra job that accepts start/end timestamps + account id; produces a signed tar.gz that contains: logs.csv, kv-snapshot.json, traces.pb
2) Encryption: support wrapping the tar.gz with customer KMS (we'll call external KMS during packaging); fallback is double-encrypt (Redwood KMS + S3 server-side) if customer KMS not available at packaging time
3) Delivery: put artifact into a pre-authorized S3 bucket in the customer's cloud; log transfer in audit ledger and include signed receipt
4) Destruction: after retention window closes, we run a coordinated destroy job; generate a signed destruction attestation and optionally annotation in the customer's audit ledger

Engineering asks:
- We'll need a small API surface (internal-only) for requesting bundles (POST /ops/bundles) and a job that signs artifacts. Time estimate: 2 sprints including Q/A if we narrow scope to pilot accounts only.
- For BYOK handoff: we need an onboarding flow that can accept a customer public key or KMS ARN and validate it before packaging.

Open product question for backlog triage: do we gate this behind a Dedicated/Private plan or provide a limited hosted pilot path? If we gate it, we can avoid extra KMS surface area but it impacts go-to-market for pilot customers.

—Kimberly
Director, Compliance Engineering
Redwood Inference


On Thu, 08 Oct 2026 09:08:43 -0700 irene_choi@redwood.ai wrote:
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marucs_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: David Ramos <dramos@helixhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 09:08:43 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary longer audit window for pilot + access model

Folks —

A few compliance points to capture before we approve the pilot exception:
- Evidence integrity: we must include a verifiable chain-of-custody header in the bundle (signed digest + packaging attestation).
- Minimal PII retention: prefer pseudonymized data and a clear mapping table stored only in Helix's KMS; Redwood should not retain mapping after handoff.
- Access controls: use short-lived pre-signed URLs with restricted source IP and VPC rules where possible.
- Audit of the auditor: Helix must provide an internal point-of-contact and SLA for handling access requests; we will require onboarding approval from our legal/compliance team.

Please treat the above as gating criteria. If we can agree to an MOU that includes the destruction attestation and chain-of-custody, I'm comfortable greenlighting a pilot exception.

Irene Choi
Head of Security Compliance, Redwood Inference
